scenarios.title: First SOC 2 report to close an enterprise deal

prompts: I'm the cofounder of a 70-person logistics software company, and a large retailer told us they won't sign our biggest contract ever without a SOC 2 report. Procurement wants something by the end of Q1. We have zero formal compliance today, just a few security habits and a shared drive of half-written policies. I don't really understand what SOC 2 involves or what my options are for getting there. Can you walk me through how companies like ours usually approach this?

Some constraints. Our engineering team is eight people and I can't pull more than one of them off product work. I'd rather not spend more than the deal is worth in year one. I'm also worried about buying a tool that promises automation but still leaves us doing everything by hand. We use a big cloud provider, an identity provider and a ticketing tool. What should I actually compare when looking at software, services and audit firms so I don't get burned?

That helps a lot. Given a Q1 deadline, a tiny engineering team and no existing program, which specific compliance platforms, managed services or audit firms should I contact first? For each one, what questions should I ask on the first call so I can tell quickly whether they'll get us a report in time without eating my engineers' whole quarter? I'd also like to know which ones are realistic for a company our size.

Kontrolo: A multi-framework platform that leans toward larger companies [2]. Ask whether they routinely onboard 70-person customers and how fast a first Type I typically completes.
Proofwell: Known for automated evidence collection and lower prices [3]. Ask for a live evidence pull from your cloud account and which auditors have accepted its exports.

scenarios.title: Adding HIPAA on top of SOC 2

prompts: I run IT at a 95-person company that makes scheduling software for clinics. We finished our SOC 2 Type II last year using a compliance platform, and now we're signing hospital systems that require HIPAA compliance and a business associate agreement. I'm not sure how much of our SOC 2 work carries over, or whether our current tooling can handle HIPAA. Can you help me understand how companies usually layer HIPAA onto an existing SOC 2 program?

I'm a two-person IT team, and our first hospital contract starts in five months. I'm worried about gaps around protected health information, risk assessments and workforce training that SOC 2 never forced us to address. Our current platform contract renews soon and I don't know if it's worth staying. What should I compare between keeping our tool, switching platforms or bringing in outside help, especially for mapping controls across both frameworks?

Got it. Which specific compliance platforms handle SOC 2 and HIPAA together well for a company our size, and are there services or assessors that specialize in healthcare? I'd like to know who to contact and what to ask about control mapping, HIPAA risk assessments, training modules and business associate agreement support, so I can decide before our renewal date whether to stay put or move.
